items_missed: Never asked for the caller's name — the lead is captured only as a phone number
No 'how are you today?', no agenda statement, no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never asked for a target move date or timeframe

Almost no structured probing: no addresses or zips beyond 'central Houston' to 'Frisco', no stairs/floors, no garage or storage rooms, no special considerations, no box count, no storage stops, no additional stops, no access/parking concerns, no stressor question. Home size and packing needs only came up because the customer volunteered them

Contradictory pricing: opened with '$208 an hour... two movers one truck', then said a 2500 sqft home is 'usually five movers, two trucks', then quoted '$100 a mover an hour. It's $200 for two movers' — the customer had to restate the math back twice to pin it down, and never got a 5-mover number
Did not itemize what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap, pads, bands, tools)
Packing pricing given as hourly but materials cost never mentioned
No Meet Your Mover, no On-Time Guarantee
Insurance covered as bare '$2,000 insurance coverage' — no No Worries name, no repair/replace/reimburse framing, no 60c/lb baseline
Clock section skipped — no on-site start, no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped on an explicitly budget-driven call
No booking attempt and no next step — closed with 'we hope you choose us next time' and let a self-identified comparison shopper hang up with no name, no email, and no follow-up scheduled
Stated operating hours as '8:00 AM and 6:30 AM'
Mentioned the long-distance job is 'a different scope for another specialist on the team' but never offered to connect him or take his info for that handoff
top_strength: Strong on the long-distance structure question the customer actually called about — she explained the two-day/overnight model, the roughly 3.5-4 hour Houston-to-DFW drive, that the drive is billed hourly rather than as a trip fee, and gave usable packing time ranges for both full-house (7-8 hrs) and kitchen-only (2.5-3.5 hrs). The Carrollton/Frisco exchange built real rapport and the customer left saying it was 'very helpful.'
coaching_note: This was a warm, winnable lead that walked away uncaptured — get the caller's name and email and offer to send the ballpark in writing, even on a 'very preliminary' call. Second, tighten the rate delivery: quoting $208/hr, then five movers and two trucks, then $200 for two movers in the same breath forced the customer to do the math for you and left the actual 2500 sqft number unstated.
phone_presence_notes: Genuinely warm and conversational — met the customer's 'vague request' framing without defensiveness and built real rapport over Frisco/Carrollton, with the customer volunteering 'that's very helpful' and 'I'm sure I'll be calling you all back.'
audio_review_reason: The pricing segments transcribe inconsistently ($208 vs $200 vs $100/mover, '78 hours', '8:00 AM and 6:30 AM') — audio needed to confirm whether the rep actually gave the customer conflicting rate figures or the transcript garbled them, since it materially affects the Pricing and Estimate scores.
